protocol.description:
This protocol allows clients to render three-dimensional content that the compositor composites, together with content from other clients, into one shared, depth-tested space presented on a head-mounted display.
A client renders its content from compositor-supplied view and projection matrices and submits, for every view, a colour image and a depth image as one atomic frame. The compositor resolves visibility between clients using the submitted depth. Geometry never crosses the wire; the compositor never re-renders client content, and clients never learn the composed result.
This protocol continues the zxr_shell_unstable_v1 protocol of the wxrc compositor, which itself descended from the Motorcar research compositor. The per-view model, the surface role, and the typed colour/depth buffer distinction survive from version 1; the folded model-view-projection matrix event and the composite wl_buffer wrapper do not.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the experimental phase. Backward incompatible changes may be added without bumping the major version of the extension. As such, gating usage on the protocol's presence is discouraged outside spatial-os itself.

interface.name: zxr_shell_v2
interface.description:
The global entry point. It advertises the compositor's transport and format capabilities, assigns the XR surface role, and creates the per-client timing and input objects.
Capability, format, and transport events are sent when the client binds the global and whenever the supported set changes, always terminated by a done event.

entry.name: role
entry.summary: given wl_surface already has another role

entry.name: defunct_surfaces
entry.summary: shell destroyed before its child objects

entry.name: missing_capability
entry.summary: request requires a capability that was not advertised

enum.name: capability
enum.description: Optional capabilities of the compositor. Requests that require a capability the compositor has not advertised raise the missing_capability error, since a client able to inspect the capabilities event has no reason to issue them.

enum.name: transport
enum.description: How image contents reach the compositor. Every compositor must accept shm; dmabuf is the intended production transport. The meaning of the submitted images is identical on every transport.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the shell object. This request must be sent after destroying all objects created through it; otherwise the defunct_surfaces error is raised. Objects created through other globals are not affected.

request.name: get_xr_surface
request.description:
Create a zxr_surface_v2 role object for the given surface. If the surface already has a role or a role object of any kind, the role error is raised.
The wl_surface is put into the XR role: attaching a wl_buffer to it with wl_surface.attach raises the zxr_surface_v2.buffer_forbidden error, since image content is carried exclusively by frame slots.

request.name: get_frame_timing
request.description: Create the per-client frame timing object delivering frame snapshots and presentation feedback. At most one timing object may exist per client shell binding; a second request raises the role error.

request.name: get_ray
request.description: Create a zxr_ray_v2 object for the given seat. Requires the ray capability.

request.name: get_pointer_6dof
request.description: Create a zxr_pointer_6dof_v2 object for the given seat. Requires the pointer_6dof capability.

event.name: capabilities
event.description: The capabilities of the compositor, as a bitfield of capability entries. Clients should hide or disable the UI elements that depend on absent capabilities.

event.name: depth_format
event.description: One supported depth image format, as a DRM FOURCC format code. Sent once per supported format. Colour formats are negotiated through the transport's own mechanism (wl_shm.format, zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1 feedback); depth formats are advertised here because neither transport distinguishes depth from colour.

event.name: transport
event.description: One supported transport tier. Sent once per supported tier.

event.name: done

description.summary: all pending shell state has been sent

event.description: Sent after the capability, depth_format, and transport events on bind and after any later change. This allows changes to the shell state to be seen as atomic, even if they happen via multiple events.

interface.name: zxr_view_v2
interface.description:
A view is one perspective the compositor composes — typically one eye of a head-mounted display. Each view is advertised as one global. A client renders one colour and one depth image per view it binds.
The view's slowly-changing properties (resolution, field of view) arrive through events on this object, terminated by done. Per-frame view and projection matrices never arrive here; they are part of the atomic frame snapshot on zxr_frame_timing_v2, so that matrices and images can never pair across frames.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Release the client's binding. Frame slots holding attachments for this view are not affected; their images for this view are ignored at submission.

event.name: resolution
event.description: The recommended pixel size for images rendered for this view. A client may submit other sizes; the compositor scales, at a quality cost. Values set in this way take effect for slots submitted after the following done event.

event.name: fov
event.description: The field of view of this view, expressed as the tangents of the four half-angles from the view's optical axis. Informational: the authoritative projection arrives in each frame snapshot.

event.name: done

description.summary: all pending view state has been sent

event.description: Sent after resolution and fov on bind and after any later change. This allows changes to the view state to be seen as atomic, even if they happen via multiple events.

event.name: finished

description.summary: the view will no longer be composed

event.description: Sent when the compositor removes the view (for example, the display configuration changed). The compositor will immediately consider the object inert. Any requests will be ignored except the destroy request; there won't be any more events referencing this object. Frame slots referencing the view remain valid; their attachments for this view are ignored at submission.

interface.name: zxr_surface_v2
interface.description:
The XR role object for a wl_surface. The surface's content is defined exclusively by submitted frame slots; wl_surface.attach is forbidden on surfaces with this role.
The compositor assigns the surface a bounding volume and a world transform. The client must render its content inside the configured bounds, in its own model space; the compositor clips content that escapes the bounds according to the clipping mode. Bounds changes follow the configure/ack pattern: the configured state should not be applied immediately, but only when the client is ready to render within it.

entry.name: unconfigured
entry.summary: frame submitted before the first ack_configure

entry.name: incomplete_slot
entry.summary: submitted slot lacks a required image

entry.name: stale_frame
entry.summary: submitted frame id was never announced or already presented

enum.name: clipping_mode
enum.description: How the compositor treats fragments whose position falls outside the configured bounds. In cuboid mode the bounds behave as a solid box: escaping fragments are discarded. In portal mode the bounds behave as a window into a volume behind its front face; fragments are discarded only outside the portal frustum. The compositor enforces clipping regardless of client cooperation.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the role object. The wl_surface loses the XR role and may be given another. Frame slots created from this surface become inert.

request.name: set_clipping_mode
request.description: Set the clipping mode. Values set in this way are double-buffered relative to frame submission: the mode applies to slots submitted after this request.

request.name: ack_configure
request.description: Acknowledge the configure event with the given serial. The client must acknowledge the latest received configure before its next submit; submitting against an unacknowledged bounds change is not an error, but the compositor clips against the configured bounds it last acknowledged. Acknowledging a serial the compositor never sent raises the invalid_ack error.

request.name: create_slot
request.description: Create a frame slot: a reusable container for the per-view colour and depth images of one frame. Clients typically create two or three slots and cycle them as the compositor releases them.

request.name: submit
request.description:
Atomically submit the slot's images as this surface's content for the announced frame with the given id. The slot must contain a colour and a depth image for every view the client has bound that is not finished; otherwise the incomplete_slot error is raised. The frame id must be one announced on zxr_frame_timing_v2 and not yet presented; otherwise the stale_frame error is raised. Submitting before the first ack_configure raises the unconfigured error.
The images, the depth metadata, the acquire points, and the frame id form one atomic unit. A slot that has been submitted must not be written to until its released event; the effect of such writes on composed output is undefined unless the transport's acquire points order them.
If the compositor's composition deadline for the named frame has passed, the submission is not an error: the compositor presents the surface's previously presented content for that frame and reports the outcome through frame feedback.

arg.name: frame_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the frame id

arg.name: frame_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the frame id

event.name: configure
event.description: Suggest a new bounding volume for the surface, as half-extents from the surface origin along its local axes. The configured state should not be applied immediately; the client acknowledges with ack_configure and renders within the new bounds from its next submission.

arg.name: half_width
arg.summary: half extent in metres, local x

arg.name: half_height
arg.summary: half extent in metres, local y

arg.name: half_depth
arg.summary: half extent in metres, local z

interface.name: zxr_frame_slot_v2
interface.description:
A reusable container holding, per view, one colour image, one depth image, their explicit-sync acquire points, and the depth encoding metadata. Attachments accumulate in the slot and become the surface's content only through zxr_surface_v2.submit; there is no per-image visibility on screen.
Depth images carry window-space depth as produced by the client's projection; the metadata request maps stored values to view-space distances so that depth from different clients is comparable.

entry.name: unknown_view
entry.summary: view object not created from this client's binding

entry.name: busy
entry.summary: slot written to between submit and released

entry.name: invalid_metadata
entry.summary: depth metadata values out of range

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the slot. Attached wl_buffers are not affected and remain valid. If the slot is submitted and not yet released, the compositor's use of the images continues until its internal release; the released event is not sent.

request.name: attach
request.description:
Attach a wl_buffer as the image of the given type for the given view, replacing any previous attachment of that (view, type) pair. A null buffer removes the attachment. Attaching to a slot that is submitted and not yet released raises the busy error. Attaching for a view not bound by this client raises the unknown_view error.
Depth buffers must use a format advertised through zxr_shell_v2.depth_format.

request.name: set_acquire_point

description.summary: set the acquire timeline point for one image

request.description:
Set the timeline point that must be signalled before the compositor may sample from the image attached for the given (view, type) pair. The timeline is a DRM syncobj; the 64-bit point is combined from point_hi and point_lo. Acquire points are consumed by the next submit and must be set again for the next use of the slot.
On the shm transport this request is ignored.

request.name: set_depth_range

description.summary: set the depth encoding for one view

request.description:
Define how stored depth values for the given view map to view-space distance: the stored value range [min_depth, max_depth] maps to the distance range [near, far] metres, linearly in reciprocal distance. If the reversed flag is set, min_depth corresponds to far. min_depth and max_depth must lie in [0, 1] and near must be positive and less than far; otherwise the invalid_metadata error is raised.
This state is consumed by the next submit, together with the attachments it describes.

event.name: released

description.summary: the compositor is done with the slot

event.description: Sent when the compositor has finished all sampling from the slot's images for the last submission. The client may reuse or rewrite the images. Release points on the images' timelines, where the transport provides them, are signalled no later than this event; the event may arrive out of submission order across different slots.

interface.name: zxr_frame_timing_v2
interface.description:
Delivers, once per compositor frame, the atomic snapshot a client needs to render that frame: the frame id, the predicted display time, the submission cutoff, the per-view view and projection matrices, and the world transform of each of the client's XR surfaces. The snapshot is terminated by a done event; all state between frame and done belongs to the named frame. This allows the matrices, transforms, and timing of a frame to be seen as atomic, even if they happen via multiple events.
Matrices are column-major arrays of 16 IEEE 754 binary32 values in native endianness. Positions and axes follow the compositor's convention: metres, y up, right-handed.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the timing object. Pending feedback objects are not affected.

request.name: feedback

description.summary: request feedback for the next submission

request.description: Request presentation feedback for the given surface's next submit. The feedback object delivers exactly one presented or discarded event and is then destroyed by the compositor.

event.name: clock
event.description: Tells the client in which clock domain the compositor interprets and produces the timestamps of this interface, as a POSIX clockid_t. Sent once, immediately after creating the object. The compositor should prefer a clock which does not jump and is not slewed.

event.name: frame
event.description: Announces a frame. The display time is the predicted time the frame's light reaches the user's eyes, as seconds combined from tv_sec_hi and tv_sec_lo plus tv_nsec nanoseconds; tv_nsec must be in [0, 999999999]. The cutoff is the duration before the display time by which submissions for this frame must arrive to be composed; later submissions are treated as described in zxr_surface_v2.submit. The period is the compositor's current frame period.

arg.name: frame_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the frame id

arg.name: frame_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the frame id

arg.name: tv_sec_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the display time seconds

arg.name: tv_sec_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the display time seconds

arg.name: cutoff_ns
arg.summary: submission cutoff before display time, nanoseconds

event.name: view_state

description.summary: per-view matrices for the announced frame

event.description: The view and projection matrices of one view, valid exactly for the frame announced by the preceding frame event. Rendering with matrices from any other frame produces misaligned composition; clients must pair these matrices with the frame id at submit.

event.name: transform

description.summary: a surface's world transform for the frame

event.description: The model-to-world transform of one of the client's XR surfaces for the announced frame. The client renders in its model space; the compositor composes using this transform, so a client need not — and must not — bake it into its projection.

event.name: done
event.description: Ends the snapshot of the frame announced by the preceding frame event.

arg.name: frame_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the frame id

arg.name: frame_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the frame id

interface.name: zxr_frame_feedback_v2
interface.description: Delivers the outcome of one submission. Exactly one of presented or discarded is sent, after which the compositor destroys the object.

event.name: presented
event.description: The submission was composed into the frame with the given id and reached the display at the given time, in the clock domain of zxr_frame_timing_v2.clock. tv_nsec must be in [0, 999999999].

arg.name: frame_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the frame id

arg.name: frame_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the frame id

arg.name: tv_sec_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the presentation time seconds

arg.name: tv_sec_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the presentation time seconds

event.name: discarded
event.description: The submission missed its frame and its content was never displayed.

interface.name: zxr_ray_v2
interface.description:
A pointing ray, following the wl_pointer model: focus is conveyed by enter and leave, motion is delivered in surface-local terms, and logically grouped events are terminated by a frame event.
Ray origins and directions are arrays of 3 IEEE 754 binary32 values in native endianness, in the focused surface's model space, in metres; directions are unit length.

event.name: enter
event.description: The ray has entered the surface's bounds and the surface gains ray focus.

arg.name: direction
arg.summary: 3 binary32 values, native endianness, unit length

event.name: leave
event.description: Ray focus left the surface. The leave event is sent before the enter event for any new focus.

event.name: motion
event.description: The ray moved within the focused surface. The timestamp is in the domain of zxr_frame_timing_v2.clock, in milliseconds.

arg.name: direction
arg.summary: 3 binary32 values, native endianness, unit length

event.name: button
event.description: A button on the ray's device changed state. The button code is a linux/input-event-codes.h code.

event.name: frame

description.summary: end of a logical event group

event.description: Groups the preceding events into one logical hardware event.

interface.name: zxr_pointer_6dof_v2

description.summary: six degree of freedom pointer device

interface.description: A tracked pointer with position and orientation, following the same focus and frame model as zxr_ray_v2. Positions are arrays of 3 IEEE 754 binary32 values in native endianness, surface-local, metres; orientations are arrays of 4 binary32 values forming a unit quaternion in x, y, z, w order.

event.name: enter
event.description: The pointer entered the surface's bounds and the surface gains pointer focus.

arg.name: orientation
arg.summary: 4 binary32 values, unit quaternion, x y z w

event.name: leave
event.description: Pointer focus left the surface. The leave event is sent before the enter event for any new focus.

event.name: motion
event.description: The pointer moved within the focused surface. The timestamp is in the domain of zxr_frame_timing_v2.clock, in milliseconds.

arg.name: orientation
arg.summary: 4 binary32 values, unit quaternion, x y z w

event.name: button
event.description: A button on the pointer's device changed state. The button code is a linux/input-event-codes.h code.

event.name: frame

description.summary: end of a logical event group

event.description: Groups the preceding events into one logical hardware event.
